must_contain: COMPLIANCE IS MANDATORY FOR NASA EMPLOYEES
Responsible Office: Office of Protective Services
Effective Date: June 06, 2025
Expiration Date: June 06, 2030
Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI)
Reciprocity of National Security Investigations and Adjudications
Appendix C: References

This NPR prescribes personnel security program responsibilities and procedural requirements for personnel security investigations, determinations of eligibility for access to Classified National Security Information (CNSI) and to hold a sensitive position, continuous evaluation, contractor fitness, adjudication, and appeals of NASA Federal and contractor employees.
This NASA directive applies to NASA Headquarters and all NASA Centers, including Component Facilities and Technical and Service Support Centers.
This directive applies to the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, a Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), only to the extent specified in the NASA/Caltech prime contract.

This directive is applicable to other contractors, recipients of grants and cooperative agreements, or parties to other agreements only to the extent specified or referenced in the applicable contracts, grants, or agreements.
In this directive, all document citations are assumed to be the latest version unless otherwise noted.
National and Commercial Space Programs, 51 United States Code (U.S.C.)
Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. 552.
NPR 1441.1, NASA Records Retention Schedules.
Whistleblower Protection: Appellate Review of Retaliation Regarding Security Clearances and Access Determinations.
National Industrial Security Program: Industrial Security Procedures for Government Activities, August 1, 2018.
Measurement of compliance will rely upon objective and modern analytic methods rather than practices that avoid risk.
NPR 1600.3A, Personnel Security, dated August 3, 2020.

Strong personnel security processes and practices, adhering to Federal requirements and guidance, support a secure environment where trusted individuals are granted appropriate access to approved assets to conduct business.
NASA requirements for suitability are outlined in NPR 3730.1, NASA Suitability Program.
The NASA Administrator shall implement a comprehensive and effective personnel security program for the Agency.
Serve as the Agency Advocate for the investigative and adjudicative systems of record.
Serve as the Agency Administrator and primary point of contact to DCSA, ODNI, and OPM.
Oversee the fitness determinations of all NASA contractors.
Review and assess compliance with personnel security requirements for the Agency.
Process and submit all background investigation requests electronically using the investigative questionnaire system of record.
Process requests for eligibility for access to CNSI or to occupy a sensitive position.
Conduct National Criminal History Checks (NCHC) and other local records checks or automated record checks, as appropriate.
The NASA General Counsel shall provide legal counsel as required within this policy.
that provides fines or imprisonment for not more than 1 year, or both.
Individuals who perform work for or on behalf of the Agency shall be assigned to a position which has been designated in accordance with OPM position designation requirements.
Intergovernmental Personnel Act (IPA) personnel will be adjudicated for access based on their position designation.
The Identity Management and Account Exchange (IdMAX) system will be the authoritative system for tracking, initiating, and adjudicating investigations.
OCHCO will assign position risk and sensitivity level designations to civil service employees in coordination with their supervisor and PSD.
The position risk and sensitivity level for contractor positions will be identified and specified in the contract statement of work.

notes: NPR 1600.3B, Personnel Security, effective June 06, 2025 (26 pages as served by NODIS, letter size, iText 2.1.0, untagged; Last-Modified September 4, 2025, a later regeneration of the NODIS PDF; NODIS lists the directive with effective date 6/6/25), cut to pages 1-13 with pypdf. Pages 1-2: masthead and table of contents; pages 3-4: Preface (P.1-P.6); pages 5-7: Chapter 1; pages 8-13: Chapter 2 (2.1-2.10). Page 14 starts 'Chapter 3. Personnel Security for Sensitive Positions', and pages 15 and 16 begin with the numbered paragraphs 3.1.13 and 3.4.5 (no new heading), so 13 is the largest k of at most 15 at whose end a section ends. Not checked: the NASA logo (image), the NODIS link line and the masthead words 'NASA Procedural Requirements' (set over three lines beside the logo). Headings: the table of contents sets 'Table of Contents', 'Preface', the chapter titles and the appendix titles as headings (large bold), and its chapter titles differ from the body: 'Chapter 2. Personnel Security Investigations and Adjudications' (contents) vs '... Background Investigations ...' (body), and 'Chapter 3. ... for National Security Positions' (contents; the body chapter is not kept); both chapter-2 forms are listed; 'Preface' and 'Chapter 1. Introduction' are printed as headings on both the contents page and the body page and are listed once (the one-to-one match needs one heading line). The body headings are listed with their typed numbers as printed ('P.1 Purpose', '2.10 Personnel Security File Storage and Access'); '2.4 Non-U.S. Citizens' is not listed (hyphen). The large bold subject lines of page 1 ('Personnel Security', 'Responsible Office: ...') are not listed as headings ('Personnel Security' occurs inside many headings); the responsible-office line is a phrase. The numbered paragraphs (1.1.1, 2.6.7 'Changes in Position, Risk, or Sensitivity Level', 2.9.5 'Adverse Information.') are plain text, not headings. Tables: none. must_contain: 47 phrases, each printed once in the kept pages (contents entries were used only where the body section is not kept), none crossing a page break; list labels ('a.', '1.3.2') are left out of the phrases. Phrases avoid every hyphen ('Agency-wide', 'high-level', 'non-sensitive', 'NASA-sponsored'), the curly quotation marks of P.2 d and 2.2, the apostrophes ('Agency's', 'employee's') and the section signs. The phrase 'NPR 1600.4, Identity and Credential Management.' is not used because 2.1.3 prints it again. ordered: 8 anchors on pages 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Noise: every page prints the footer disclaimer ('This document does not bind the public, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract. This document is uncontrolled when printed. Check the NASA Online Directives Information System (NODIS) Library to verify that this is the current version before use: https://nodis3.gsfc.nasa.gov.') and 'NPR 1600.3B -- <part>' in both the header and the footer (26 times in the kept pages); neither occurs in the body (the masthead prints 'NPR 1600.3B' without '--'); max 1 each (one kept copy is tolerated). The '--' is assumed to be two ASCII hyphen-minus characters; if it is another code point the entry simply counts nothing for every tool. 'Page N of 26' differs per page and is not counted. Absent: the text is ragged-right; its line-end hyphens are in compounds ('higher- or lower-risk'), so absent is empty. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 70-300 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, seals, signatures, chart art) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
